subject: Social Media
title: The Right to Be Forgotten
description: A quick win: understand The Right to Be Forgotten.

hook.text: A Spanish man's old debt showed up on Google for years after he paid it. He sued—and won a new legal right.

buildup.text: In 2014, the EU ruled people can ask Google to delist outdated personal results. Over 1.5 million requests followed.

discovery.text: Google approves about 45% of requests. The rest are denied—public interest outweighs personal privacy claims.

twist.text: The U.S. has no such right. Americans can't remove true but outdated results. Your past is always searchable.

climax.text: Forgetting is human. The internet doesn't forget. The law is still catching up to digital memory.

punchline.text: Humans forget. Search engines remember forever.

quiz.question: What percentage of 'right to be forgotten' requests does Google approve?
